provenance.orgName: Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk, Benedictine abbey of St Edmund, King and Martyr
provenance.p: This attribution has had a complex history in Medieval Libraries of Great Britain.
In the first edition (1941), there is no reference to MS Hunter 7 in connection with Bury.

In the second edition (1964), the shelfmark is listed with a positive Bury attribution in the index of manuscripts (p. 350). However, the manuscript is not included in the main Bury section of the 'List of Surviving Books' in the second edition (pp. 16-22).

Between the publication of the second edition (1964) and the Supplement (1987), see for comparison R. M. Thompson, 'The Library of Bury St. Edmunds Abbey [...]', Speculum 47 (1972), p. 618 n. 3: a number of Bury MSS have been added to Ker's 1964 list, which for the sake of convenience I list here [...] Glasgow, University Library MS Hunterian 7(?) [italics in this quotation supplied here for emphasis].

In the Supplement (1987), MS Hunter 7 is rejected under Bury in the 'List of Surviving Books' and the index of manuscripts (pp. 7, 122). In both locations, the attribution is presented as new rather than revised. In other words, the Supplement does not reflect the fact that a Bury attribution was previously accepted in 1964 (or, more specifically, was accepted in the index only in 1964).

No corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card was found during data reconciliation work in 2026. In all likelihood, the card would once have cited the following passage from John Young and Patrick Henderson Aitken, A catalogue of the manuscripts in the Library of the Hunterian Museum in the University of Glasgow (Glasgow, 1908), p. 11:

p.q: On iii, 2 rᵒ in the same hand [xvii century]: John Gower | De Confessione Amantis. Imprinted at London in Flete strete | by Thomas Berthelette the | xii daie of Marche. An MDLIIII. | Cum Privilegio | This Book as I was told by the Gent: who presented it to me did originally belong to the Abby of Bury in Suffolk. Prof. G. C. Macaulay (Clarendon Press Edition of John Gower's Complete Works, Oxford, 1901), remarks on this: If so, the Confessio Amantis was probably the copy read by Lydgate.

provenance.p: Compare, more recently, Linne Mooney and Derek Pearsall, A descriptive catalogue of the English manuscripts of John Gower's Confessio amantis (Cambridge, 2021), p. 74: None of the additions to the MS provide evidence of provenance.
